new_findings.title: G16 returns PASS under a name its own detail contradicts, and freezes a tree-specific fact as a rule
new_findings.detail: the check is named DECLARED_COVERS_IMPORTS; its detail prints declared_covers_imports=False; the code (gate_w0r9.py:350-372) passes when the artifact honestly reports the undeclared set. Worse: it returns CRYPTOGRAPHY_FALSELY_MARKED_UNDECLARED when 'cryptography' appears in the undeclared set, so on worktrees/r4-hgk (deps=[]) the correct measurement is marked red.
new_findings.fix: rename to REPORT_STATES_UNDECLARED_SET, drop the cryptography assertion, and let the measured value travel with its ref

new_findings.title: G13 is a dead assertion: the gate reads a key the artifact never writes
new_findings.detail: gate reads duplicate_digest_groups / duplicate_digests; lanes/A/AUTHORITY_CONFLICT_LEDGER_V2.json writes duplicate_sha256_groups. Setting the real field to 4 still yields PASS 'in-set dup=0'.
new_findings.fix: read duplicate_sha256_groups; fail closed when the key is absent

new_findings.title: G10 resolves a nested chapter's parent claim, not the document's own
new_findings.detail: the chain for r9 is r5 -> r6 -> r7 -> r9; r8 is not in the chain list at all, and the resolved declaration (264787b0, r7) is the one printed inside r9's r8 chapter. r9's own declared parent (ccd545b5, r8) was never checked. The prefix claim itself is true (I verified byte equality), so this is a gate-coverage defect, not a document defect.
new_findings.fix: resolve the declaration belonging to the document under test; report DECLARED_PARENT_NOT_IN_CHAIN when it is absent from the chain

new_findings.title: G18 containment is a string prefix test
new_findings.detail: gate_w0r9.py:133 uses fp.startswith(base); a sibling directory sharing the prefix (../r9-evil/) satisfies it. Symlinks are not resolved.
new_findings.fix: use os.path.commonpath on realpath, and fail closed on an empty manifest
